verdicts.reading: In 2006 the soccer World Cup will be the first major global sporting event offered in high definition.

evidence.shows: All 64 matches originated in HDTV; first major international sports event to fully commit to HD production.

verdicts.reading: The number of blogs worldwide exceeds 60 million during 2006.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Quantitative (D10/D16): blogs tracked worldwide around end-2006 against >60 million.
verdicts.reason: Technorati, the standard blog census of the time, went from 35 to 75 million blogs in 320 days and tracked over 70 million by April 2007, with about 120,000 new blogs a day; the count passed 60 million around the turn of 2006/07. Technorati counts all blogs, not only personal ones, so the fit is approximate but within 10%.

evidence.title: The State of the Live Web, April 2007 (Dave Sifry, Technorati)
evidence.shows: Over 70 million weblogs tracked; about 120,000 new weblogs a day; 35 to 75 million in 320 days.

verdicts.reading: Aggregate paid-for telecom connections (mobile, fixed lines, broadband) exceed four billion worldwide in 2006.

verdicts.reason: ITU: 2,744.6 million mobile, 1,260.9 million fixed telephone and 284 million fixed broadband subscriptions in 2006, about 4.29 billion in total. Mobile added about 539 million in the year, matching the half-billion side claim.

evidence.title: ITU regional and global key ICT indicator aggregates (Nov 2025)
evidence.shows: World 2006: mobile 2744.6m (2005: 2205.3m), fixed telephone 1260.9m, fixed broadband 284m.

verdicts.reading: In 2006 3G subscribers grow by tens of millions while 2G/2.5G remains the majority of mobile subscribers, revenues and growth.

verdicts.reason: By June 2007 only about 200 million 3G subscribers existed, 6.7% of 3 billion subscriptions, so 3G grew by tens of millions while 2G remained the overwhelming majority; total mobile grew by about 540 million in 2006, nearly all 2G.

evidence.title: 3G (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: 200 millionth 3G subscriber by June 2007, 6.7% of 3 billion subscriptions.

evidence.title: ITU regional and global key ICT indicator aggregates (Nov 2025)
evidence.shows: World mobile subscriptions 2205.3m (2005) to 2744.6m (2006).

verdicts.reading: In 2006 several premium brands from outside telecoms launch their own branded phones.

verdicts.reason: The best-known case, the LG Prada phone, was announced on 12 December 2006 but released only in March 2007; Armani and other designer phones also came in 2007. The trend arrived, but the launches fell mostly a year late.

evidence.title: LG Prada (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: First announced 12 December 2006; released in UK, France, Italy in March 2007.

verdicts.reading: In 2006 the telecom industry largely overlooks machine (M2M) connections as a source of growth.

evidence.title: ITU regional and global key ICT indicator aggregates (Nov 2025)

verdicts.reading: In 2006 operators' race to higher broadband speeds does not translate into profit growth.

evidence.title: ITU regional and global key ICT indicator aggregates (Nov 2025)
evidence.shows: Fixed broadband grew from 219.6m (2005) to 284m (2006) subscriptions; no profitability data.

verdicts.reading: Telecoms undergoes a period of intense M&A activity in 2006.

evidence.title: O2 (UK) (Wikipedia)

verdicts.reading: In 2006 fixed operators fail to capture their full share of convergence revenues.
